title: Local-mode cost simulator toolkit — spec & quickstart (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a small, pragmatic prototype spec and quickstart for a local-mode cost/latency simulation toolkit aimed at SDK authors and integrators. Goal: let engineers estimate unit economics (token cost, p99 latency impact, autoscaling pressure) for a feature without attaching to hosted billing or spinning up Dedicated capacity.

Why we need it (context):
- Onboarding SDK users frequently ask: "how much will this cost in production?"
- Running full traffic on Hosted consumes credits and can be slow to iterate.
- Developer flows (local dev, CI) need repeatable, deterministic workloads for regressions and perf testing.

Principles:
- Small, opinionated surface: CLI + single config file + optional small Python lib.
- Fast feedback: simulate at the request level using sampled token/latency distributions derived from real telemetry.
- Economically meaningful: output per-endpoint and per-prompt cost estimates using current pricing profiles.
- Reproducible: checkpointed sample prompt sets and seedable generators.
- Safe: explicit disclaimer about divergence from production (caching, batching, KV state).

Quickstart (2–3 minutes):
1) Install (local virtualenv):
   pip install -e ./local-sim  # dev install from repo

2) Create a config file (sim-config.yaml):
   model: gpt-small-384
   quant: q4_0
   pricing_profile: hosted-v1
   rps: 20
   avg_prompt_tokens: 120
   prompt_set: examples/quickstart-prompts.json

3) Run a single-shot simulation:
   ri-local-sim run --config sim-config.yaml --seed 42 --out out/quickstart-report.json

4) View report (human):
   ri-local-sim summarize out/quickstart-report.json

What the toolkit actually does (implementation sketch):
- Load a prompt set (JSON array) and a model profile. Model profile includes: nominal throughput (tokens/sec), token-cost-per-unit, kv-cache-hit-rate heuristics, and a small latency distribution (p50/p90/p99) per prefix-length bucket.
- For each request: sample tokenization (token count) from a fitted empirical distribution; sample generation latency from the model's latency distribution (option to add network overhead).
- Apply batching simulation: configurable batching window and max batch size; simulate how batching would change average latency and throughput.
- Apply caching heuristics: reuse KV cache on prompt prefix matches above threshold; compute effective tokens generated vs cached tokens.
- Compute cost: token-unit * token-count * pricing-profile multipliers + optional infra estimate for Dedicated (GPU-hours estimate).
- Emit traces: per-request synthetic trace with labels for "cached", "batched", "quantized", and pointers to the input prompt id.

CLI examples and knobs:
- ri-local-sim run --model gpt-small --rps 50 --duration 60 --prompt-set examples/email-prompts.json
- ri-local-sim run --config sim-config.yaml --burst 200 --q8 --route-policy fallback:small->tiny
- ri-local-sim profile --compare hosted-baseline.json --delta out/experimental.json

Expected outputs:
- report.json (flat fields): total_tokens, billed_tokens, avg_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, estimated_cost_usd, simulated_rps_peak, autoscale_signal_strength
- csv of per-request events (timestamp, prompt_id, tokens, latency_ms, batch_id, cache_hit)
- histogram PNGs for token counts and latencies (optional)

Sample pitfalls / caveats (to call out explicitly in docs):
- Not a replacement for full e2e bench: real infra (GPU kernels, memory pressure, NUMA) can change latency profiles drastically.
- Caching and KV semantics in multi-turn chat are simplified.
- Pricing profiles must be regularly updated (linked to billing table).
- Synthetic prompt sets can bias results; provide recommended prompt sets per vertical.

Telemetry contract suggestions (for SDK integration):
- Exported signals from simulation: sim.run_id, seed, model_profile, pricing_profile, prompt_set_id, duration_sec, total_requests, total_tokens, billed_tokens, estimated_cost_usd.
- Provide an opt-in uploader for anonymous aggregated reports to help product refine model profiles (GDPR-safe).

Developer checklist (pre-merge):
- [ ] Add minimal Python API: run_sim(config) -> dict(report).
- [ ] Add seedable synthetic prompt generators for: conversational, completion, instruction, summarization.
- [ ] Add a small set of vetted prompt_set JSON files under examples/ (quickstart, email, search-snippets, support-chat).
- [ ] Wire pricing table to repo/config and mark source of truth (billing repo or console).
- [ ] Add CI smoke test to run quickstart under GitHub Actions (fast, deterministic seed).

Open questions / decisions:
- Should the sim ship as part of the SDK packages or as a separate dev-tool repo? Tradeoff: discoverability vs release cadence.
- How closely should simulated batching match runtime (continuous batching vs fixed-window)?
- Safety: do we include any sample PII prompts for realistic testing? Prefer sanitized examples.

Roadmap (next 3 sprints):
- Sprint 1: prototype CLI + YAML config + quickstart prompt sets + 1 example pricing profile.
- Sprint 2: add batching model + cache heuristics + Python API + GH Action smoke test.
- Sprint 3: integrate model profiles derived from hosted telemetry (sampled) + reliability notes + small UX writeup for Console.

Notes to reviewers / TODOs:
- Priya to provide a small starter pricing_profile JSON (approx. hosted-v1).
- Evan to draft the GH Action workflow for CI smoke test.
- Marcus to pull p99 latency buckets from hosted telemetry (anonymized) and provide two model-profile examples (small, medium).

Appendix: sample minimal prompt_set file (examples/quickstart-prompts.json)
[
  {
    "id": "q1",
    "text": "Write a short marketing blurb for a developer-first inference platform."
  },
  {
    "id": "q2",
    "text": "Summarize the following customer support ticket into three action items."
  }
]
